q: For a linear map T: V → V on a finite-dimensional space, the Cayley-Hamilton theorem can be used to show the minimal polynomial m_T divides the characteristic polynomial p_T. This means the minimal polynomial:
opts: Has the same roots as p_T but possibly smaller degree
Has strictly smaller degree than p_T
exp: The minimal polynomial m_T has the same roots (eigenvalues) as p_T but each may appear with smaller multiplicity. m_T | p_T by CH. A matrix is diagonalizable iff m_T has no repeated roots (all eigenvalues appear with multiplicity 1 in m_T).
